attempts.summary: Configured node1, node2, node3 as a 3-member MariaDB Galera cluster (mariadb-server-galera 10.5.29, galera 26.4.22 from RHEL 9 AppStream). Bootstrapped node1 via galera_new_cluster, joined node2 and node3 via SST (mariabackup). Had to fix a SELinux AVC denial (mysqld_t self connectto on unix_stream_socket, required for the mariabackup SST donor/joiner) by loading a small local policy module (mysqld_sst.pp) on all three nodes. Opened firewalld ports 3306/4444/4567(tcp+udp)/4568 on all nodes. Verified writes from any of the three members replicate synchronously to the other two. Demonstrated availability during a member outage: stopped node3, cluster stayed Primary with 2/3 quorum and accepted writes; on node3 restart it auto-resynced via IST and picked up the write made while it was down. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id + healthy Synced/Primary status + data on each node, restarted node1, node2, then node3 one at a time via `systemctl reboot` (backgrounded so the ack returned first), polled each until reachable again, confirmed changed boot_id, and confirmed each rejoined as Synced/Primary with cluster_size 3 and correct data after every restart, only proceeding to the next node once full health/quorum was restored. Final cross-node write/read check after all restarts confirms consistent replication. Root and SST credentials were generated on node1 with openssl and distributed to node2/node3 over cluster SSH; not included in this report (the SST password did appear in one earlier debug `cat` command's tool output, but was not reused or logged further).
